title: Cloudastructure Announces Reverse Stock Split
body_text: PALO ALTO, Calif., July 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Cloudastructure, Inc. (Nasdaq: CSAI) , a provider of AI-powered video surveillance, remote monitoring, and cloud-based security analytics, today announced that its stockholders have approved, and the Company intends to effect, a reverse stock split of its Class A Common Stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the “Common Stock”), at a ratio of 1-for-30, to become effective on July 31, 2026. Following the reverse stock split, the Common Stock will continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol “CSAI,” with a new CUSIP number of 18912E306. No fractional shares will be issued in connection with the reverse stock split. Any fractional shares will be rounded up to the nearest whole share. Proportionate adjustments will be made to the number of shares of Common Stock issuable upon the exercise or conversion of the Company’s outstanding equity awards, warrants and other convertible securities, as well as to the applicable exercise or conversion prices. The reverse stock split is intended to increase the per share trading price of the Common Stock in order to regain and maintain compliance with the $1.00 minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2). The Company’s transfer agent, Transfer Online, Inc., is acting as exchange agent for the reverse stock split. Stockholders holding shares in book-entry form or through a bank, broker or other nominee are not required to take any action in connection with the reverse stock split. About Cloudastructure Headquartered in Palo Alto, California, Cloudastructure’s patented, advanced, award-winning security platform utilizes a scalable cloud-based architecture that features cloud video surveillance with proprietary, state-of-the-art AI/ML analytics, and a seamless remote guarding solution. The combination enables enterprise businesses to achieve proactive, end-to-end security, and pairs that platform with an attractive value proposition that eschews proprietary hardware and offers contract-free, month-to-month pricing and unlimited 24/7 support. With Cloudastructure, companies can achieve unparalleled situational awareness in real time and thereby stop crime as it is happening, while simultaneously achieving up to a 75% lower Total Cost of Ownership than other systems. For more information, visit https://www.cloudastructure.com/ . Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements Certain statements in this press release may be considered forward-looking. Any forward-looking statement expressing an expectation or belief as to one or more future events is expressed in good faith and believed to be reasonable. However, these statements are not guarantees of future events and involve risks, uncertainties and other factors beyond our control including our ability to effect the reverse stock split on the expected terms and within the expected timeframe, whether the reverse stock split will have the intended effect of increasing the per share trading price of our Common Stock or enabling us to regain and maintain compliance with Nasdaq’s minimum bid price requirement, and general market and economic conditions. We caution you against relying on any of the forward-looking statements in this release, as actual outcomes and results may differ materially from what is expressed in any forward-looking statement. Except as required by applicable law, we do not intend to update any of the forward-looking statements to conform them to actual results or revised expectations. Media Contact Kathleen Hannon, Sr. Communications Director Cloudastructure, Inc. 704.574.3732 Kathleen@cloudastructure.com Investor Contact Valter Pinto, Managing Director KCSA Strategic Communications 212.896.1254 Cloudastructure@KCSA.com ‍

title: Genpact Launches Banking Analyst Suite, Agentic AI for Regulated Banking Operations
summary: Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst, the first module, now generally available for AML alert investigations NEW YORK, July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Genpact (NYSE: G), an agentic and advanced...
body_text: Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst, the first module, now generally available for AML alert investigations NEW YORK , July 23, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- Genpact (NYSE: G), an agentic and advanced technology solutions company, today announced Genpact Banking Analyst Suite , an enterprise solution that applies agentic AI to regulated banking operations. Its first module, Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst , is now generally available to help banks complete routine anti-money laundering (AML) alert investigations faster and more consistently, and with human oversight and full auditability. Built on Genpact's experience running financial crime operations for many of the world's leading institutions, including reviews of millions of alerts annually, the solution uses AI agents modeled after how AML investigations are conducted at scale. Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst coordinates AI agents to assess customer behavior, analyze transactions, validate profiles, review prior alerts, and recommend next steps. Analysts make the final decisions; the system does not take regulated action without human approval. Financial institutions face rising alert volumes, increasingly sophisticated financial crime, and intensifying regulatory scrutiny. Compliance teams need to clear high volumes of low-risk alerts quickly and consistently, without weakening the governance and defensibility regulators require. Unlike tools that only score alerts, Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst completes the first-level investigation workflow and delivers a decision-ready recommendation with documented rationale and a detailed audit trail for analyst review. "What sets Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst apart is the operating expertise behind the AI," said Satish Acharya, Service Line Leader, Financial Crime & Risk Management, Genpact. "We have run financial crime programs for some of the world's largest financial institutions, and we have built that knowledge into how these AI agents investigate. This solution helps analysts shift time from repetitive alert work to the higher-risk cases where human judgment matters most." Expected outcomes for AML investigations For in-scope AML alert investigations, the solution is expected to deliver: Faster reviews: up to 80% lower handling time for in-scope investigations Lower cost: up to 40% lower total cost of ownership Stronger investigations: more consistent, defensible reviews, with a documented rationale and audit trail for every recommendation Expanding the suite Genpact plans to extend Banking Analyst Suite across additional regulated banking workflows, including customer due diligence, screening, fraud , customer service, and other risk areas. The suite will be designed to support the governance, data isolation, information security, and system integration requirements of regulated environments. For institutions using Genpact's riskCanvas® financial crime platform, Banking Analyst Suite will run natively alongside riskCanvas®. AMP Limited , an Australia- and New Zealand-based financial services company, is among the first to deploy Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst. "At AMP, protecting customers and strengthening operational resilience are critical priorities," said Sean O'Malley, Group Executive, AMP Bank . "By combining Genpact's Banking Analyst Suite with riskCanvas®, we are equipping our teams with tools that help streamline investigations, improve consistency, and accelerate case resolution. As financial crime risks continue to evolve, agentic AI offers significant potential to reduce manual effort, enhance analyst productivity, and enable greater focus on complex cases that require human expertise." To learn more about Genpact Banking Analyst Suite and Genpact Transaction Monitoring Analyst , visit genpact.com. Projected outcomes are indicative and vary by client environment, operating model, data quality, and implementation scope. About Genpact Genpact (NYSE: G) is an agentic and advanced technology solutions company. We leverage process intelligence and artificial intelligence to deliver measurable outcomes. With a strong partner ecosystem and decades of client trust, we provide innovative solutions that transform how businesses run. Powered by a team with an active learning mindset and client-centricity at its core, we deliver lasting value for the world's leading enterprises. Get to know us at genpact.com and on LinkedIn , YouTube , X , and Facebook . MEDIA CONTACT: Sue Martenson Genpact Media Relations +1-978-905-9582 susan.martenson@genpact.com SOURCE Genpact

title: AI revenue automation: What it is and how to get started
summary: See how AI revenue automation unifies pricing, billing, and revenue recognition so complexity fuels growth instead of slowing finance down
body_text: Every SaaS and AI company hits the same wall eventually. The pricing model that worked at $1M ARR starts creaking, and by the time you're mixing seats, usage, and credits across a few hundred contracts, your finance team is spending more time reconciling spreadsheets than closing the books. What you have on your hands is a systems problem. Because the companies pulling ahead right now aren't the ones with the simplest pricing. They're the ones whose revenue stack, pricing, quoting, billing, collections, and revenue recognition, can absorb that complexity without breaking . AI revenue automation is what makes that possible. Used well, it doesn't just cut down on manual work. It turns pricing flexibility into a genuine growth lever instead of an operational tax. In this guide, we'll break down what AI revenue automation actually looks like in practice, where it shows up across the revenue cycle, and a practical path to building it, so pricing changes accelerate growth instead of slowing your finance team down. What is AI revenue automation? ℹ️ AI revenue automation refers to using AI-powered software to handle the tasks and processes involved in getting paid. It includes recommending or configuring pricing, generating and approving quotes, rating usage data, matching payments, predicting late invoices, and applying revenue recognition rules to complex or changing contracts. AI revenue automation is a step beyond "traditional" revenue automation , which mostly relies on predefined rules and templates. AI-based systems can interpret unstructured inputs (a contract clause, a support ticket, a payment history pattern), adapt to exceptions, and make judgment calls that would otherwise land on a finance analyst's desk. AI revenue automation covers the following: Pricing and packaging: Recommending price points, tiers, or discount guardrails based on deal and usage data CPQ and quoting: Configuring complex, multi-element quotes and flagging non-standard terms for review Billing and usage metering: Rating usage events and catching anomalies before they hit an invoice Invoicing and collections: Predicting payment risk, prioritizing outreach, and automating dunning sequences Revenue recognition: Reading contract terms, detecting amendments, and updating recognition schedules automatically Where AI shows up across the revenue cycle AI revenue automation isn't confined to one system. Here's how it typically breaks down across the quote-to-cash cycle . Revenue cycle stage What AI typically automates Example Pricing and quoting Configuring quotes for hybrid pricing, flagging non-standard discounts A rep quotes a mix of seats and usage credits without looping in RevOps Billing and usage metering Rating usage events in real time, catching metering anomalies A spike in API calls is flagged before it becomes a disputed invoice Invoicing and collections Predicting late payments, prioritizing and automating dunning High-risk accounts get proactive outreach before an invoice is overdue Revenue recognition Reading contract terms, detecting amendments, updating schedules A mid-term upsell automatically recalculates the recognition schedule Revenue reporting Surfacing anomalies in MRR, ARR, and churn without manual pulls A dashboard flags an unexpected drop in expansion revenue same-day How to get started with AI revenue automation Where to actually begin can be the toughest question to answer. Do you start with pricing and quoting? Or do you hand billing over to an AI-driven engine first? Or tackle collections because that's where the manual hours are piling up right now? Trying to automate everything at once is usually how these projects stall out before they deliver anything. The good news is that getting started doesn't require a full rip and replace of your finance stack. But what it does require is a clear-eyed look at where your current process breaks down, a realistic pilot, and a platform that can grow with you as you automate more of the quote-to-cash cycle. Most teams that get this right start small, prove the value on one workflow, and expand from there. Map your current revenue workflow: Document how a deal moves from quote to cash today, including every handoff between sales, finance, and engineering. Identify repetitive, rule-based tasks: Look for tasks that follow a pattern but still require manual execution: matching payments, updating recognition schedules, or re-keying contract terms into a billing system. Evaluate platforms by workflow, not just feature list: Compare how each platform actually handles your pricing model, whether that's a dedicated CPQ implementation, a billing engine, or an end-to-end quote-to-cash system. Pilot on a defined segment: Roll out AI automation to a subset of accounts or a single product line before switching your entire revenue operation over. Train your team and set governance: Make sure finance and RevOps understand what the system automates, what it escalates, and who owns the exceptions. Track outcomes and iterate: Revisit the goals you set at the start. Adjust thresholds, escalation rules, and scope based on what the data shows after the first full billing cycle. How Alguna approaches AI revenue automation Alguna is a venture backed AI revenue automation platform for AI, SaaS, and fintech companies. Pricing, quoting, billing, and revenue recognition run on the same data, making sure everyone's looking at the same numbers. The platform is built modularly, meaning you don't have to rip our your entire revenue stack to get started. For example, if CPQ is your biggest pain point, Alguna's no-code CPQ can be implemented in weeks and get you up and running, making use of Contracts AI to speed up the quoting process. It supports complex pricing structures out of the box, including tiered, seat-based, usage-based models, outcome-based , and hybrid pricing , without engineering involvement. On the billing side, usage events are ingested and rated automatically, and the accounts receivable AI agent handles the chasing, so you don't have to worry about payment collections. On the finance side, automating revenue recognition means contract amendments, renewals, and upsells trigger recalculated schedules and journal entries automatically, in line with ASC 606 and IFRS 15. This kind of end-to-end approach matters because AI monetization strategies tend to change quickly as products and usage patterns evolve. Power your growth with AI revenue automation AI revenue automation isn't a single feature you switch on. It's a shift in how pricing, billing, collections, and revenue recognition work together, so pricing complexity becomes something your revenue stack absorbs rather than something your finance team fights every month. Start with the workflow causing the most friction today, whether that's SaaS invoicing or your revenue recognition close, and expand from there. Get that foundation right and every new pricing experiment becomes a growth lever instead of a finance fire drill. If you're comparing platforms more broadly, our roundup of automated revenue management solutions is a good next stop.

title: Don't Click That Text: Recognizing Text Scams
summary: Updates, insights, and stories to feed your financial growth and showcase client success.
body_text: Don't Click That Text: Recognizing Text Scams Financial Well-Being Text scams are rising as criminals shift from phone calls to messages that appear to come from trusted sources like your bank, the court system, or even federal agencies. They use fear and urgency to push you into sharing personal information. Whether the message claims there’s fraud on your account, you missed jury duty, or a government agent needs to speak with you, the goal is always to steal your money. How Text Scams Work: Scammers often send alarming messages that appear to come from official sources. Some common tactics include: Bank or Account Alert Scams: These messages urge you to click a link or reply with personal information such as your account number, PIN, or password. Examples of texts you may receive: "Fraudulent transaction detected." "Your account will be locked if you don't..." "Immediate verification required." Jury Duty or Law Enforcement Scams: They often demand payment through untraceable methods like gift cards, wire transfers, or cryptocurrency. Some scammers pose as court officials or police officers, claiming: "You missed jury duty. Pay now to avoid arrest." "Failure to show up to jury duty requires a fine; pay here" Fake Government Agent Scams: Scammers impersonate FTC agents or federal authorities, even sending fake badge numbers or ID photos to appear credible. They may claim your identity is at risk and pressure you to transfer money "for safekeeping." "Your identity has been compromised. An arrest warrant will be issued if you fail to respond..." "Your name appeared in a federal investigation involving identity theft. To secure your assets, please transfer your funds immediately. Reply YES to receive instructions." Signs It's a Scam Be alert if you notice any of these red flags: Urgent or threatening language designed to make you act fast Requests for personal or financial information via text Links that don’t match official websites Messages sent from a 10-digit phone number instead of an official five-digit short code Southern First will only send messages from our verified five-digit number. What To Do If You Receive a Suspicious Text Do NOT click any links or reply. Verify using a trusted source. Call the number on the back of your debit card or log in through our official mobile app or website. Report the scam by forwarding the message to 7726 (SPAM) and call Southern First’s Fraud Department at 864-679-9646. If you shared any information, immediately change your online and mobile banking password, monitor your accounts for suspicious activity, and report anything unusual. Delete the message once reported to avoid accidental clicks later. Your security is our priority. Our team proactively monitors your accounts to help detect unusual activity and protect you from potential fraud. We are committed to keeping you informed and educated on the best practices to safeguard your personal information. Banking with Southern First means having a partner you can trust every step of the way. Southern First will never ask for your password, PIN, verification, or Social Security number via text message. If something feels off, trust your gut and contact us directly. Our Insights, Your Inbox Sign up for thoughts and perspectives from the Southern First team Newsletter Signup

title: Promissory Notes: Your Frequently Asked Questions
summary: Find out what a promissory note is, when to use one, and what it should include. Get clear answers to common questions in this simple legal guide.
body_text: ❓What is a promissory note? A promissory note is a written agreement in which you, as a borrower, promise to repay a specific amount of money plus any agreed-upon interest to a lender. This document serves as a formal contract, and it outlines your commitment and creates a legal obligation. It’s issued by you, the borrower, and provided to the lender as a signed promise to repay, making it enforceable if you fail to meet its terms. It’s not just an IOU, it details repayment schedules, interest rates, and maturity dates, offering clarity and accountability for both parties. In U.S. law, a valid promissory note may qualify as a negotiable instrument under the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) , meaning it can be transferred or negotiated like a financial instrument. ❓When should you use a promissory note? You should use a promissory note any time you’re lending or borrowing money where repayment is expected. Whether it’s a personal loan between family or friends, a business transaction, or a mortgage, a promissory note offers legal clarity. For informal smaller amounts, you might proceed without one, but if you want enforceable repayment terms, especially for larger sums, it’s essential. Even for personal loans, it reduces misunderstandings and helps you outline a clear schedule of payments, interest, and consequences for default. In the event you need to collect unpaid debt, having a written contract is enormously valuable. ❓ What types of promissory notes exist? Promissory notes come in various forms depending on how repayment is structured: Simple note : Covers the basics, such as amount, interest, and payment schedule. Secured note : You pledge collateral (like a car) that the lender can seize if you default. Unsecured note : No collateral is required, but you’re still legally bound to pay. Master note : Often used in student or commercial lending, this serves as a standing agreement for multiple future loans. Open-ended note : Used in revolving credit setups, this lets you draw and repay funds over time without creating new notes. Demand note : Payment is due whenever the lender demands it. Balloon note : Involves smaller periodic payments and one large final payment at the end. ❓What must be included in your promissory note? To ensure it’s legally sound, make sure your promissory note includes: Your and the lender’s names and contact info Principal amount borrowed Interest rate details Payment schedule and due dates Maturity date (when full repayment is due) Any fees, taxes, or penalties Issue date and location Your signature as the borrower (the lender may also sign for added clarity These components ensure clarity, enforceability, and protection for both parties. Depending on your agreement, you can include additional terms as needed. ❓How are promissory notes used in business? Promissory notes are common in business transactions for loans involving land, vehicles, equipment, working capital, or intercompany lending. They’re especially useful when you need formal proof of a loan agreement along with legal recourse for repayment. By including collateral or specific repayment terms, you protect your interests and reduce the risks associated with business loans. For businesses, promissory notes provide a structured way to manage debt, more robust than informal IOUs, and easier to enforce if repayment issues arise. ❓How can you sign promissory notes electronically? You don’t need paper and pen to make your promissory note binding. With tools like ROGER or other e-signature platforms, you can sign digitally, easily save a copy, and securely store it in the cloud. This allows you and the lender to complete the entire process remotely, with fewer delays. Under U.S. laws like the E-SIGN Act and UETA , electronic signatures carry the same legal weight as handwritten ones. That makes digital promissory notes a fast, compliant, and efficient solution. ❓Why use a promissory note instead of an IOU? An IOU simply acknowledges that you owe money, but it lacks detail about repayment terms and provides little legal protection. In contrast, a promissory note spells out repayment schedules, interest terms, collateral (if any), and maturity date. It offers a stronger legal foundation and may qualify as a negotiable instrument under U.S. law. If repayment disputes arise, the lender can use the note in court to enforce the agreement, something an informal IOU can’t reliably support. ❓Is a promissory note legally binding? Yes, a promissory note is legally binding, as long as it includes the essential elements of a valid contract. These typically include identification of both parties, the amount borrowed, repayment terms, interest rate (if applicable), and your signature. Once the note is signed, you are legally obligated to repay the loan under the agreed terms. If you fail to follow the agreement, the lender can pursue legal action to recover the debt. It’s important to treat promissory notes with the same seriousness as any formal loan agreement. Even in personal lending situations, having everything in writing offers protection and clarity for both sides. ❓What happens if you default on a promissory note? If you default, meaning you fail to meet the repayment terms, you could face serious consequences. The lender may issue a notice of default and give you a final chance to pay. If that fails, they may file a lawsuit, which could lead to a court judgment, wage garnishment, or asset seizure, especially if the note is secured by collateral. In business orlarge personal loans, defaulting can also damage your credit and future borrowing capacity. If you signed a secured note, the lender may repossess the pledged item (e.g., car, equipment, or property). For demand or balloon notes, failing to pay the full balance when requested can trigger immediate collection efforts. To avoid default, always communicate with your lender if you run into financial trouble. Many lenders are open to modifying repayment schedules if they’re kept in the loop. title: How to Send Money from Ghana to UAE in 2026: A Practical Guide
summary: A practical guide to sending money from Ghana to the UAE in 2026.
body_text: A Ghanaian business owner sent me a voice note a few weeks ago. She had been trying to pay a supplier in Dubai and had already gone through three different services in six weeks. One transfer sat pending for nine days. One arrived short because of a rate markup she never saw coming. One got rejected entirely because the receiving bank needed a document type she had never encountered before. She wasn't asking me to overhaul her whole setup. She just wanted to know: what actually works on the Ghana-UAE corridor? I've been thinking about that question since. This guide is my answer. Why This Corridor Is Busier Than Most People Think Tens of thousands of Ghanaians live and work in the UAE, concentrated in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Some are professionals, some are business owners, many are keeping families afloat back home in Accra and Kumasi. But the corridor isn't just diaspora remittances. Ghana's trading relationship with the UAE has grown substantially over the past decade. UAE-based wholesale markets, particularly for electronics, textiles, and food products, have become a regular sourcing point for Ghanaian importers. There is a real and growing stream of business payments moving in this direction, and most of those payments are still being done the expensive way. This week, the Central Bank of Nigeria announced it is targeting $1 billion in monthly diaspora remittances by year-end, up from around $600 million per month now. Nigeria gets most of the attention in these conversations, but the broader trend cuts across West Africa. The Gulf corridor is where African money is moving in 2026, and Ghana is a meaningful part of that story. Ghana's cedi went through a brutal stretch after 2022. The IMF stabilization program helped, and the GHS has found a more stable footing over the past 18 months, but the volatility of those years taught a lot of Ghanaian senders something important: the exchange rate matters as much as the fee. That lesson is directly relevant to anyone sending money from Ghana to the UAE today. The Part Most People Get Wrong I want to be direct about the most common mistake, because it costs people real money every time. Most senders look at the fee and stop there. "$3.99 flat transfer fee" sounds cheap. But the fee is only one cost in this transaction. The exchange rate markup is the other, and it is often larger. The mid-market rate is the real exchange rate at any given moment, the one you'll find on Google or XE.com. What most apps actually charge you is that rate minus a margin, usually somewhere between 0.5% and 2.5% depending on the provider and the corridor. On a $500 transfer, that looks like $2.50 to $12.50 in hidden cost. People fixate on the $3.99 fee and walk right past the $10 rate spread. The only way to catch this is to check what the mid-market rate is at the time you are sending, then compare it to the rate the app is actually offering you. The second thing people get wrong is not checking transfer limits before they commit to a service. Most consumer-focused fintech apps cap individual transactions somewhere between $1,000 and $5,000, with monthly cumulative limits that vary by verification level. For personal remittances, that usually isn't a problem. For business payments to Dubai suppliers, it can become one fast. Find out the limit before you build a payment routine around an app, not after. What Actually Works on This Corridor in 2026 The UAE dirham has been pegged to the US dollar at 3.67 since 1997. That peg has held through everything. It means that when you send money from Ghana to the UAE, what you are really asking is: how efficiently can this service convert my cedis to dollars and move those dollars to the UAE? The AED destination is predictable. The GHS-USD step is where the spread lives. For personal remittances, the digital transfer apps have caught up. Services like Afriex, Wise, and WorldRemit all cover the Ghana-UAE corridor, and the delivery times to UAE bank accounts have improved considerably. Wise in particular is transparent about its rate markup, which I respect even when it isn't the cheapest option, because at least you know what you are paying. My habit with any service I haven't used on a specific corridor is to do a test comparison: enter the exact amount I want to send, note the "recipient gets" figure, then back-calculate what effective exchange rate that implies and compare it to mid-market. That comparison tells you more than any marketing copy. For business payments, the calculus is different. You probably need to move more money per transaction, you want a proper receipt for your records, and the timeline has to be reliable because suppliers in Dubai do not wait around indefinitely. For these reasons, the pure-consumer apps may not be the right fit. Some fintech platforms are building specifically for SME cross-border payments and offer higher limits with cleaner documentation. It is worth looking at your options in that segment if your transfers regularly exceed $2,000. What I would not do is default to a wire transfer through a Ghanaian high-street bank. The fees are real: most local bank international SWIFT transfers run between $25 and $50 per transaction, and that is before the recipient's UAE bank potentially charges an incoming wire fee. On a $500 supplier payment, that fee structure is simply not defensible when the alternatives exist. One practical approach for businesses with multiple UAE suppliers: batch your payments. Instead of sending five separate transfers to five suppliers, consolidate and send once. Most platforms support multiple recipients within a single transaction, or at minimum let you send to the same account repeatedly at lower friction. One transfer means one set of fees, one rate to negotiate, one compliance check instead of five. Before You Send: What You'll Need UAE bank accounts use IBAN format for international transfers. This is a requirement, not a preference. If your recipient gives you just an account number without the IBAN, ask them for it explicitly. You'll also need the receiving bank's SWIFT/BIC code and the bank's address. Most UAE banks will have this on their website or on a statement. If you are sending through a fintech app, confirm that the service delivers directly to UAE bank accounts in the first step, not just to cash pickup locations. Many consumer apps started with cash pickup networks and are still building out their bank-to-bank coverage. A cash pickup works fine if your recipient prefers it, but if they need it in their bank account, verify the delivery method before you commit. For transfers above a certain threshold, you will be asked to provide source of funds documentation. The exact threshold varies by provider and by Ghana's current regulatory requirements under FATF guidelines. This is not arbitrary friction. It is part of what makes legitimate transfer channels trustworthy, and services that skip this step entirely are a warning sign, not a convenience. Have a bank statement or payslip ready if you are moving a meaningful amount. The Timing Question The UAE business week runs Sunday through Thursday. Banks are closed on Friday and Saturday. If you are making a business payment and you send on a Thursday afternoon in Accra, that transfer may not clear into a UAE bank account until Sunday Dubai time. For personal remittances to family, timing usually matters less. For supplier payments with a deadline, it matters a lot. Fintech app transfers are generally faster than traditional wire transfers because the mechanics work differently: the platform holds funds at both ends and settles between them, rather than moving actual correspondent bank transfers in real time. That architecture is why transfer times on modern apps have come down to hours rather than days on most corridors. On the rate side, the GHS does tend to experience mild pressure during peak import seasons as demand for foreign exchange picks up. I'm not suggesting you try to time every transfer like a currency trade. But if you send regularly and have flexibility on timing, paying attention to where the cedi is trading against the dollar in a given week is not paranoia. It is just being financially sensible. For Business Owners Sourcing From Dubai If you are a Ghanaian importer who sources goods from the UAE wholesale markets, there is one habit I'd encourage above everything else on this list: know your effective landed cost. That means knowing not just the supplier price in AED, but exactly how much it will cost you in cedis by the time the payment clears, after the transfer fee, the rate margin, and any receiving charges. Most importers calculate this loosely and are slightly surprised each time. The ones who track it closely find the savings over the course of a year. I'd also encourage you to compare options specifically on your typical transaction size. The service that is cheapest for a $200 personal remittance may not be the cheapest for a $3,000 supplier payment. Fee structures differ at different amounts. Run the comparison at your actual number. The Short Version The Ghana-UAE corridor has real, functional options in 2026. The fintech infrastructure exists. What you owe yourself before each transfer is three minutes of comparison: check the mid-market rate, check what the app will actually deliver to your recipient after all costs, and pick the one that wins on that specific transaction. The difference compounds over time if you are sending regularly, and the money you save on rate margins and fees is yours to keep.

title: PwC Scales Model ML AI Agents Globally
body_text: Model ML today announced that PwC and Model ML have been co-developing AI capabilities, now being scaled globally across PwC. Over the past several months, the two teams have worked in close partnership to co-create a suite of AI solutions side by side. Together, Model ML and PwC have developed a combination of off-the-shelf and custom agents designed to support transaction-related work and streamline the review of PwC documents. PwC selected Model ML following its demonstrated velocity, commitment, and collaborative approach, with feedback frequently reflected in the platform within hours. Because Model ML is model-agnostic, each task is routed to the model best suited to the dimension that matters most, whether a frontier model or a faster, lower-cost open-source model running on Model ML's infrastructure or within PwC's own environment, across every surface the team works on. "A huge thank you to Dan, Colin, Toby, Joseph and the wider PwC team. It's rare to see a firm this size move so decisively on AI, and rarer still to get to build it with them," said Chaz Englander, CEO of Model ML.
